7. Icons

An icon is a line drawing in the same hand as the mark: square-edged, one weight, no fill.

How an Icon Is Drawn

  • On a 16-unit grid, with a stroke of 1.5 and miter joins.
  • NCode's own drawings end a line in a butt cap. An icon taken from Lucide ends it in a square cap: Lucide draws each line for a cap that reaches half the stroke past its end, and draws a dot as a line 0.01 units long, which a butt cap does not show.
  • One stroke weight; no fill, except a dot NCode draws as a small circle.
  • The line is 1.5 pixels at every size: every stroked shape in icons/ carries vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke", so a 20-pixel icon is drawn as finely as a 16-pixel one.
  • The color is currentColor, so an icon takes the color of the text beside it.

The Set

icons/ holds each icon three ways: icons/<name>.svg alone, a symbol i-<name> in icons/sprite.svg, and its shapes in icons/icons.json, for a component that draws it inline. build.mjs draws NCode's icons from src/icons/ncode.svg. It takes Lucide's from the files src/icons/lucide.lock.json pins by SHA-256, scales each from Lucide's 24-unit grid to 16, and draws it to the rules above.

Drawn byLine endsIcons
NCode, in src/icons/ncode.svgButt capsarrow-left, arrow-right, arrow-up-right, building, caution, check, chevron-down, chevron-left, chevron-right, chip, clients, close, cloud, copy, device, edit, error, eye, file, globe, info, key, layers, lock, menu, moon, people, pin, plus, recycle, scope, search, server, shield, sign-out, sliders, success, sun, trash, user, zero
Lucide 1.72.0, restyledSquare capsactivity, bell, calendar, circle-question-mark, clock, code, database, download, ellipsis, ellipsis-vertical, fingerprint-pattern, funnel, git-branch, link, log-in, mail, minus, package, qr-code, refresh-cw, rotate-ccw-clock, settings, terminal, upload

One source draws each name: Lucide supplies only icons NCode does not draw, and the build stops on a name both draw. Draw a new icon to these rules in src/icons/ncode.svg, or take one from Lucide by adding its file and its SHA-256 to the lock (the decision).

How an Icon Is Used

  • .icon is 16 pixels, for a dense interface; .icon--sm 14, .icon--lg 20 beside text of 16 pixels and above, and .icon--xl 24.
  • An icon never carries a state alone: a word sits beside it, as a lamp's does.
  • A key that holds only an icon has an accessible name, aria-label or a visually hidden word (.vh).
  • No emoji, and no icon font: a font's glyphs change with the font, and a screen reader reads them out.

Take an icon from the sprite on the page's own origin, and css/base.css gives it its size and stroke:

<svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="brand/icons/sprite.svg#i-search"/></svg>

The specimens in specimens/ take the icons each page uses from the set, in a generated block of the sprite at the top of the page, and the foundations page shows every icon of the set at 16 and 20 pixels.

License

NCode's drawings are under the Apache License 2.0, as the rest of the system is. The icons from Lucide keep Lucide's licenses: the ISC License, and the MIT License for the icons Lucide derives from Feather. Both ask every copy to carry its notice, so vendor icons/LICENSE-Lucide.txt with any Lucide icon; each Lucide file and the sprite name it.
